zzcollab Changelog

Source: CHANGELOG.md

Version history for the zzcollab CLI and template framework. R package release notes are in NEWS.md. History prior to the 0.1.0 re-baseline is archived in CHANGELOG-2.x.md.

Unreleased

Fixed

  • New projects use implicit renv snapshots. renv_init_quiet() in the .Rprofile template initialized renv with snapshot.type = "explicit", which records only DESCRIPTION’s packages. A compendium’s analysis/-only packages belong in renv.lock but not in DESCRIPTION (zzrenvcheck’s compendium rule), so they were never locked, and a renv::status() check could not see that drift. It now uses "implicit", matching the comment in zzc add that already assumed it. Existing projects keep their setting; switch one with renv::settings$snapshot.type("implicit"). Verified with renv 1.3.1: an analysis/-only package is absent from renv.lock under explicit and present under implicit.

  • make docker-build PLATFORM=... now builds for that platform. The Makefile documented ‘Override with make PLATFORM=linux/amd64’, but the build (zzc rebuild) chose --platform from uname -m and ignored it, so an amd64 image could not be built through make on an arm64 Mac, and the build and later make r could disagree. An explicit PLATFORM (command line or environment) is now passed to the build as ZZCOLLAB_PLATFORM, honored by both the build and its cache key; the auto-detected default is not passed, so the build still chooses per base image. Requesting arm64 for rocker/verse (amd64 only) is refused. A native arm64 build warns that CI builds linux/amd64 and names the CI-matching command.

  • Run targets match a rocker/verse image on arm64 hosts. The PLATFORM default was linux/arm64 on any arm64 host, while a verse image is always built linux/amd64, so make r and the other run targets requested a platform the local image did not have. The default now comes, in order, from the local image’s zzcollab.platform label (so make r runs whatever make docker-build produced, including an amd64 image built with PLATFORM=linux/amd64 on an arm64 Mac), then from the Dockerfile’s base image (verse is amd64), then from the host. make docker-rstudio, which omitted --platform, now passes it like the other run targets.

  • An unresolved base-image digest stops Dockerfile generation. When the pull failed (Docker absent, daemon down, no network), generate_dockerfile logged a warning and wrote a tag-only FROM, so the project looked pinned but was not. It now refuses and writes nothing; the new global flag --allow-unpinned (ZZCOLLAB_ALLOW_UNPINNED=true) writes the tag-only FROM with a warning for deliberate offline use, and tooling.lock records base_image_digest: null. zzc verify warns on any tag-only FROM. Commands that regenerate the Dockerfile in passing (zzc renv, zzc update) keep the existing Dockerfile and warn when this happens. Digest resolution now uses the configured runtime (podman as well as docker; apptainer resolves with docker), so a podman-only setup is not forced to --allow-unpinned.

  • zzrenvcheck is pinned, and tooling.lock tells the truth about it. tooling.lock recorded rgt47/zzrenvcheck@v0.3.1, but the image never installed zzrenvcheck: make ensure-zzrenvcheck (and make r’s post-session install) installed GitHub main unpinned, requiring only >= 0.9.0. The default tag is now v0.11.0, which is also the minimum the Makefile accepts (ZZRENVCHECK_MIN): it reads the tag from the project’s tooling.lock, uses the newer of that tag and the minimum (a lock written by an older zzcollab records v0.3.1, which lacks arguments the targets pass; the Makefile says to rerun zzc docker), and installs that release from its tag unless one at least as new is already installed. It never downgrades, so projects sharing a host library do not reinstall over each other, and a development install is kept. tooling.lock now states that the tool is installed by make ensure-zzrenvcheck (that release or newer), not into the image. Unused zzrenvcheck_tag/zzrenvcheck_version variables in the Dockerfile generator, and a generated comment naming a nonexistent make install-zzrenvcheck target, are removed.

  • Generated Dockerfiles pin OpenBLAS and MKL threads. Only OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 was set, which does not reach pthreads builds of OpenBLAS or MKL; OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 and MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 are now set too, so their reduction order, and hence floating-point results, does not depend on the host’s core count.

  • zzc verify reports a malformed renv.lock instead of aborting. The validity check’s nonzero return ended verify under set -e before its result could be reported.

  • Test gates fail when no expectation ran. TINYTEST_RUN (both Makefiles, so make test, make docker-test, make test-container, and zzc verify --full) and the test steps in r-package.yml and .gitlab-ci.yml exited 0 for a suite whose files ran no expectation, because all(logical(0)) is TRUE. They now print ‘No expectations ran’ and exit 1. Scaffolded projects ship inst/tinytest/test-basic.R with one unconditional expectation, so a new project still passes.

  • GitLab test steps are blocking. Both test steps in .gitlab-ci.yml ended in || echo "tests reported failures (non-blocking)", so a failing suite never failed the pipeline. The suffix is removed.

  • zzc verify credits a baseline only when it compared something. L3 was awarded when a test-baseline*.R file name appeared in the test log; a file that called exit_file() before any comparison is listed there with ‘0 tests’. A baseline now counts only when its final log line shows at least one test and no ‘[Exited at’ marker, so a file that exits part way also leaves the result at L2.

  • zzc verify coherence no longer aborts on generated Dockerfiles. The R-version check read ARG R_VERSION=, which generated Dockerfiles no longer write. The failed grep ended an assignment with status 1 under set -e, so with a renv.lock present zzc verify exited 1 mid-check, and the Dockerfile side of the comparison could never be read. The version is now taken from the FROM <image>:<version> tag (the ARG is still read for older Dockerfiles), so a Dockerfile whose R version disagrees with renv.lock fails coherence. zzc doctor reads the same tag when there is no renv.lock, and its state back-fill no longer aborts under set -euo pipefail when a read finds nothing (for example a renv.lock without an R section).

  • make lint fails when lintr reports anything. It printed the lints and exited 0, so it could not serve as a gate. It now exits 1 when any lint remains in R/ or analysis/; the new make lint-report keeps the old print-only behavior. A project whose code has outstanding lints will see make lint fail after zzc doctor --force refreshes its Makefile.

Changed

  • The analysis profile alias warns, and help stops recommending it. analysis is a deprecated alias for the tidyverse profile and collides with the analysis archetype. Typing it (as a profile command, with --profile, or in config set profile-name) now warns that it will be removed in the next release. A config file that already names it still maps silently to tidyverse; the removal will need to migrate those. The main help listed analysis as the recommended profile and said a profile command switches an existing project, which the code refuses; it now recommends tidyverse and points to zzcollab docker --profile NAME. make r suggested --profile analysis and labeled a tidyverse image ‘analysis’; both now say tidyverse.

  • The CITATION.cff template no longer claims all data are included. Its abstract said the compendium ‘Contains all data’, false for any deposit that withholds restricted data. It now describes the code and environment, points to the data availability statement, and a comment asks the author to edit it.

  • Both repositories ship a LICENSE.md (GPL-3, matching DESCRIPTION), so GitHub shows the license.

  • The auto-snapshot-on-exit hook is off by default. The .Rprofile .Last() hook ran renv::snapshot(prompt = FALSE) on every container R exit unless ZZCOLLAB_AUTO_SNAPSHOT was false. The Makefile already set it false for make r, the DOCKER_RUN targets, and CI, but not for make docker-rstudio or host sessions, so whether renv.lock changed depended on how R was started. The hook now defaults to off: what enters renv.lock is the analyst’s call (renv::snapshot(), make snapshot, or make fix-renv, then review the diff). Opt in with make r ZZCOLLAB_AUTO_SNAPSHOT=true (or export the variable); every container run target, now including docker-rstudio, passes the Makefile’s ZZCOLLAB_AUTO_SNAPSHOT ?= false, which also keeps a project whose .Rprofile predates this change off. make r’s post-session dependency check, which records packages the code uses, is unchanged.

  • make check-renv no longer edits files; make fix-renv repairs. check-renv, check-renv-no-strict, and check-renv-slim ran zzrenvcheck with auto_fix = TRUE: they rewrote DESCRIPTION and renv.lock and then passed, which made the target users reach for unsuitable as a CI or pre-commit gate. They now run with auto_fix = FALSE, error_on_fail = TRUE, edit nothing, exit nonzero on any finding, and name the matching repair target (fix-renv, fix-renv-no-strict, or fix-renv-slim). The repairing behavior moves to fix-renv, fix-renv-no-strict, and fix-renv-slim. check-renv-no-fix remains as a deprecated alias of check-renv; docker-check-renv and docker-check-renv-fix alias check-renv and fix-renv. make r’s post-session validation, which relies on the repair, now calls fix-renv when the host has no R. zzc validate already defaulted to no auto-fix and is unchanged. Behavior change for existing projects: after zzc doctor --force refreshes the Makefile, make check-renv fails where it used to repair silently; run make fix-renv instead.

  • Dependency checks skip a bare compendium. zzc init --bare omits DESCRIPTION by design, and zzrenvcheck (from the release that fails a project without DESCRIPTION) cannot validate one. The check-renv*, fix-renv*, snapshot (its check step), and reset-lock targets, make r‘s post-session hook, zzc validate, and zzc verify now detect a missing DESCRIPTION and report ’No DESCRIPTION (bare compendium): dependency check skipped’ with exit 0, instead of failing or passing silently. ensure-zzrenvcheck does not install the tool for a bare project. zzc verify also now runs the dependency check in the verified directory rather than the caller’s working directory.

  • render-report.yml is part of a workspace’s expected workflow set only when the workspace has a report, defined once in zzc_has_report (lib/core.sh): an .Rmd or .qmd file in analysis/report/, a report.Rmd anywhere under analysis/, or an .Rmd in analysis/posts/. Previously every non-book, non-blog workspace received it; five R-package repositories with no report spent about three minutes per CI run installing R and dependencies to log ‘Found 0 manuscripts to render’. zzc_workflow_pairs and zzc_workflow_expected take an optional workspace directory. zzc init scaffolds the archetype’s report before installing workflows, so a manuscript or analysis workspace still gets the render workflow and a package or simulation workspace does not. zzc toggle and zzc add cicd follow the same rule; enabling CI without a report offers to scaffold report.Rmd before the workflows are installed, so accepting it also installs the render workflow. zzc doctor no longer reports render-report.yml as missing when there is no report, and reports a copy found without a report as unneeded (informational, not counted as an issue, and not deleted). zzc status shows CI render off (no report) or on (no report: unneeded) in those cases, distinct from off when a report exists but the workflow is missing. When neither an R package nor a report applies, no empty .github/workflows/ directory is created.

  • r-package.yml, render-report.yml, and render-book.yml set GITHUB_PAT from the workflow’s GITHUB_TOKEN, so renv and pak resolve GitHub-hosted packages with the authenticated API rate limit rather than the 60-request hourly limit per runner IP. The token is not passed into docker build, so container image restores remain unauthenticated.

  • render-report.yml reads an optional timeout: (minutes, default 120) from .github/report-ci.yml and applies it to every render step, so a hung render fails in bounded time instead of holding the runner for the 6-hour job limit. A non-integer value fails the job with an annotation.

  • render-book.yml uses actions/cache@v6 (v4 runs on the deprecated Node 20 runtime).

Fixed (zzc update pins)

  • zzc update regenerated the Dockerfile from the renv.lock R version, the config profile, and today’s Posit snapshot, ignoring the pins in .zzcollab-state. On a publishing project it could swap rocker/verse for rocker/tidyverse (dropping TeX Live), downgrade R, and re-pin every package, despite the help text promising to keep the snapshot. It now takes the base image, R version, and snapshot from .zzcollab-state, falling back to the .Rprofile snapshot for projects without one.

Fixed (r-package.yml package repository)

  • The container check job in r-package.yml restored packages from Posit’s noble/latest binaries even when the project’s Dockerfile pins a dated snapshot, so the check could run against a different library than the image. Binaries are rebuilt against current dependencies: in missforest, Rfast 2.1.5.2 from latest is compiled against RcppParallel 6.2.1, and failed to load (undefined TBB symbol) beside the RcppParallel 5.1.11-2 that the lockfile pins to match its 2026-06-29 image. The job now takes the snapshot date from the Dockerfile’s Posit URL and uses noble/<date>, falling back to noble/latest when the Dockerfile pins none or is absent. The renv cache key includes the repository, so a cache filled from one snapshot does not seed another.

Fixed

  • The shell test suite can no longer write to the owner’s real ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml. A new tests/shell/test_isolation.sh, sourced by test_helpers.sh (so every test-*.sh run on its own) and by run_all_tests.sh, points HOME, ZZCOLLAB_CONFIG_USER_DIR, ZZCOLLAB_CONFIG_USER, the XDG_* directories, and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL into a per-process temp dir before any module loads, and removes it on exit. It also records the real config’s checksum and mtime (from the pre-isolation HOME) and fails the run with exit 3 if either changed. The leak was in test-config.sh: CONFIG_USER is readonly once modules/config.sh loads, so its export CONFIG_USER=<temp> lines failed and the fixtures and config_set calls wrote the real config. Those tests now write to the sandboxed $CONFIG_USER. run_all_tests.sh no longer aborts under set -e at the first failing suite, so it reports every suite and its summary.
  • render-book.yml (book archetype) consolidates the fixes that had been applied piecemeal across downstream books, so one unedited workflow serves every book. R packages now install only from Posit’s binary repository (an explicit CRAN repos forced source builds, and fs failed to compile for want of libuv headers, leaving rmarkdown uninstalled); a verify step, run with the project .Rprofile loaded as Quarto’s own R session is, fails the job by name when a required package is missing, since install.packages() only warns. Books without a renv.lock install knitr, rmarkdown, and any DESCRIPTION dependencies with pak (plus downlit and xml2 when code-link is on). renv books restore into the runner library with system requirements looked up per lockfile package (without re-solving the lockfile, which failed on GitHub-sourced and recommended packages), and the renv autoloader is disabled for the rest of the job so a plain source("renv/activate.R") profile cannot switch the render session to an empty project library. Install sessions run with --no-init-file, since the zzcollab .Rprofile sets CRAN source as the repository on a host. Engine detection matches only chunk fences at the start of a line, so a chunk header quoted in prose no longer provisions R. The workflow also gains the PDF edition (TinyTeX, a single all-format render, the ‘Latest PDF’ release) when a pdf format is declared, Chrome Headless Shell for Mermaid in PDF, a job timeout (90 min) and render timeout (30 min) in place of GitHub’s 360-minute default, a concurrency group, full-history checkout, a weekly scheduled run, and current action majors. Per-book differences move to an optional .github/book-ci.yml (quarto, engines, apt, backend) and optional tools/ci/pre-render and tools/ci/post-deploy hooks. Verified on 2026-11-11 across 13 Quarto books (prose, knitr with and without renv, Jupyter, Mermaid, and a Dockerfile book on the host backend): every pull request and deploy run passed.
  • One GitHub workflow set per archetype, defined once (zzc_workflow_pairs in lib/core.sh) and used by zzc init, the CI toggle, zzc doctor, and zzc update: a book carries render-book.yml, a blog post blog-render.yml, and every other compendium r-package.yml (omitted for --bare) and render-report.yml. Blog posts previously received r-package.yml and render-report.yml from zzc init, although 58 of 67 existing posts ran blog-render.yml alone; R CMD build of a post followed its dangling root figures symlink and failed. Workspaces that record no archetype are classified by the workflow they already carry, and zzc_ci_forge recognizes any of the four workflows, not only r-package.yml.
  • blog-render.yml was invalid: its check-deps job called hashFiles() in a job-level if, which GitHub rejects, so every push failed at startup. The job is removed (the render already fails on a missing package), and the workflow gains the template version header, job and step timeouts, a concurrency group, and current action majors.
  • render-report.yml reads an optional .github/report-ci.yml for reports whose data is not in git: render: skip skips every render step, skip: lists reports (paths or globs) to leave out, and reason: is shown in the run notice. The environment is still built and checked, and each skip is reported as a notice and in the step summary.
  • The r-package.yml test step loads the package (pkgload::load_all(), or a temporary-library install where pkgload is absent) before tinytest::run_test_dir(), which does not load it. Without this, any test calling a package function failed with ‘could not find function’. Deployed copies hid failures of this step behind continue-on-error: on 2026-11-12 the latest run of 34 of 71 such repositories had failed it (the one log examined, zzpower’s, failed for this reason).
  • r-package.yml runs an optional tools/ci/pre-check script before R CMD check, for per-repository setup (zzedc warms its DuckDB icu extension there) that previously required editing the workflow. render-report.yml installs libcurl, OpenSSL, and libxml2 headers on the host backend, a fix three package repositories had applied to their own copies.
  • Test targets are gates. make test, make docker-test, and the cached .make/tests-passed target now exit nonzero when any tinytest assertion fails; tinytest::run_test_dir() returns results rather than signalling, so these targets previously exited 0 (and the cached target stamped a pass) on failing tests. The CI template no longer marks the test steps continue-on-error.
  • zzc verify --full stamps L3 only when the image rebuilds, the suite passes, and a baseline test (inst/tinytest/test-baseline*.R) exists and ran. Otherwise it reports “rebuilt and tested (L2); no baseline comparison, so not L3”. A --full run that does not reach L3 removes any earlier verified= stamp, and the stamp is written to the target directory’s .zzcollab-state rather than the current directory’s.
  • get_ubuntu_codename() (and templates/tools/check-binaries.py) now follow rocker/r-ver’s actual bases: focal to 4.2.1, jammy 4.2.2 to 4.4.1, noble from 4.4.2. R 4.4.0 and 4.4.1 were mapped to noble, so the generated Dockerfile pointed PPM at binaries built for a different Ubuntu release than the image.
  • The generated Dockerfile sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.
  • The generated Dockerfile no longer embeds a build timestamp. The org.opencontainers.image.created label was written at generation time, so regenerating the file changed its text, and any hash of it (such as a simrun image tag), even when nothing else had changed. zzcollab rebuild now adds that label at build time instead. The default package snapshot (‘one day ago’) is still computed at generation time; set PPM_SNAPSHOT to pin it.
  • make sh and make r pass --no-home to Apptainer, so the host home directory (its ~/.Rprofile, user library and caches) is no longer mounted into the container. The project folder is still bound through the working directory. Not yet run against a real Apptainer install; renv’s cache under $HOME may need a writable location in that mode.
  • R started in a project subfolder now loads the project .Rprofile. make sh sets R_PROFILE_USER to the root profile, which runs from the project root while it executes and then restores the starting directory. Previously R read ./.Rprofile only from the folder it started in, so a session opened in analysis/scripts skipped the profile entirely.
  • Dependency gates pass error_on_fail = TRUE to zzrenvcheck::check_packages() (check-renv-no-fix, zzc verify’s advisory check, which previously always reported a pass), and ensure-zzrenvcheck upgrades installs older than zzrenvcheck 0.9.0. The pre-session check in the repository Makefile’s r target only reports.

Added

  • New projects get a .gitkeep in analysis/ subfolders (and docs/) that are still empty when setup ends, so a clone keeps the folders that scripts write into (derived_data/, figures/, tables/).
  • Declarative archetype scaffolding. Per-archetype scaffolding is now driven by an archetype_spec table and a single engine (apply_archetype_scaffold) with _scaffold_* entry functions, replacing ad-hoc conditionals. Adds the missing symlink primitive (create_archetype_symlinks): blog is now a single-post compendium with analysis/report/index.qmd surfaced at the root via an index.qmd symlink plus data/figures/media symlinks (matching real usage); analysis scaffolds a Quarto index.qmd (report.Rmd is now manuscript-only); book is standalone with its own media/images. New --bare flag (env ZZCOLLAB_BARE) omits the R-package skeleton and its CI workflow for prose-only compendia.
  • book research archetype for multi-chapter Quarto books. zzc init --archetype book scaffolds analysis/book/ with a book-type _quarto.yml, a preface (index.qmd), a first chapter, and references.bib; the book is excluded from the single-report.Rmd scaffold since it renders as a Quarto project. Adds a docker-render-book Makefile target and a container-backend step in render-report.yml that runs a project-level quarto render. The generated image now bakes a cwd-independent .libPaths() shim into Rprofile.site so the renv library is visible to the R sessions quarto render spawns inside analysis/book/ (which has no project .Rprofile).
  • zzc init now back-fills an existing ~/.zzcollab/config.yaml to the current schema. Older or hand-trimmed configs that lack whole sections (author, license, r_package, style, github) gain those sections with their default values and comments, while every value already set is preserved. Implemented as an idempotent deep-merge of the default skeleton under the existing file (config_backfill_schema); the merge runs only when a schema key is genuinely missing.
  • languageserver config key (default true) and a matching feature-wizard checkbox (‘R language server in Docker image (in-container LSP)’) install the R language server into the image for in-container completion and diagnostics. Opt out with zzc config set languageserver false for REPL-only workflows.
  • styler and lintr are installed in the image when the code-quality feature is active, alongside two new in-container targets: make style (format R code with styler) and make lint (lint R code with lintr).
  • publishing profile (base image rocker/verse) for manuscript rendering. It renders PDF by default when a LaTeX toolchain is present and falls back to HTML otherwise (capability-adaptive); the LaTeX package closure is pre-baked into the image at build time, so PDF rendering requires no runtime install.
  • make snapshot: capture code dependencies into renv.lock and DESCRIPTION by running, in the container, renv::hydrate(), renv::snapshot(prompt = FALSE), and zzrenvcheck::check_packages(auto_fix = TRUE, strict = TRUE). The R-package CI workflow gains a ‘Validate dependency manifest (renv.lock + DESCRIPTION)’ step that fails the build when code references a package that is not declared in DESCRIPTION or not locked in renv.lock.
  • auto_github config key (default false) and an init ‘create remote now’ wizard checkbox that it pre-selects. zzc github now walks up to the repository root before creating the remote, so it publishes the whole compendium rather than a subdirectory.
  • docs/package-placement-whitepaper.md: a comprehensive account of which packages belong in the Dockerfile versus renv.lock versus DESCRIPTION.

Changed

  • Profile analysis renamed to tidyverse. analysis is retained as a deprecated alias.

  • zzc init identity step no longer silently re-prompts only when fields are absent. When name and email are already saved, it displays the stored identity and offers an optional update, pre-filling each prompt with the current value so a bare Enter keeps it. Because zzc init is run for every new repository, the default is to keep existing values (no prompt churn); only an explicit confirmation walks the fields.

Fixed

  • config_set KEY VALUE --local (and zzc init, which uses it to record the archetype) no longer seeds a freshly created project zzcollab.yaml with an empty docker.default_profile: "" stub. The placeholder served no purpose — the loader skips empty values and the real key is written immediately after — but persisted as a meaningless override. The creation template now matches the one used by the interactive project prompt (header only).
  • tools/render.sh (via stamp-render.R) no longer fails on .qmd files inside a Quarto project. It looked only for <file>.pdf beside the source, but Quarto writes project output under the project’s output-dir, and a book renders every chapter into one PDF whichever chapter is named. The stamp now finds the new PDF under the output directory when it is not beside the source, and for a book it names the book (its project directory in the footer, its PDF title in the staged filename) rather than the chapter. Tested on a book chapter, a standalone document, and a website page.

Performance

  • The LaTeX warm-up for the publishing image now bulk-installs the package closure in a single tlmgr pass, reducing the render image build from about 7 minutes to about 2.5 minutes.

0.1.0 — 2026-06-16

Re-baseline. The CLI, the template stamp, and the R package version had drifted apart (2.8.1, 2.0.0, and 0.9.2 respectively); they are unified under a single ZZCOLLAB_VERSION source of truth in lib/constants.sh and reset to 0.1.0 to mark a new start. The earlier 2.x history is preserved in CHANGELOG-2.x.md.

This release establishes the presence-driven reproducibility-toggle architecture (see docs/reproducibility-toggle-plan-whitepaper.md).

Added

  • zzc status: read-only report of the two capture axes (backend, environment), the validation toggles, the computed level (L0-L3), and the verified stamp, read from a generated .zzcollab-state record.
  • zzc verify: a coherence tier (no build) that confirms the artifacts agree with .zzcollab-state, and a --full reproduction tier that rebuilds and tests for level L3.
  • .zzcollab-state: a generator-written provenance record, emitted by both the Dockerfile generator and zzc init.

Changed

  • The Dockerfile, .Rprofile, and the CI workflows (r-package.yml, render-report.yml) self-adapt to artifact presence: install from renv.lock when present, otherwise from DESCRIPTION; the render and check workflows fall back to a host environment when no Dockerfile is present.
  • The renv and Docker features toggle symmetrically. zzc renv / zzc rm renv and zzc docker / zzc rm docker regenerate the dependent files and reuse the remembered base image and R version from .zzcollab-state.
  • zzc doctor is toggle-aware: renv.lock and Dockerfile are reported as on/off features rather than required files, and doctor --fix back-fills a missing .zzcollab-state from artifact presence for repositories created before the record existed.

Fixed

  • zzc renv returned a spurious non-zero exit (an unconditional config prompt under set -e) and left the .Rprofile version stamp unsubstituted.
  • The shell test runner aborted silently on the first failing test; it now reports every result.
